The cybersecurity sector continues to attract strong investor interest in 2025, with venture capital (VC) funding reaching $5.1 billion year-to-date (YTD).

This surge underscores the industry’s mission-critical role as digital threats escalate and technology infrastructures expand worldwide, according to Moss Adams’ latest Cybersecurity Investment Monitor.

Investors are targeting startups delivering differentiated solutions in DevSecOps, digital identity, IoT security, and password-less authentication, reflecting the need for innovative defenses against evolving cyber risks.
Funding is balanced across seed, early, and late-stage rounds, each capturing about one-third of deal activity—evidence of a healthy pipeline from emerging innovators to scalable enterprises.
VC-backed firms are also achieving swift exits, with a median acquisition time of 4.5 years, highlighting cybersecurity’s appeal as a long-term, high-growth investment.
Private equity (PE) firms have invested $6.4 billion YTD, focusing on add-on acquisitions that now represent 57.4 percent of deal value—nearly double 2024’s share.
This consolidation trend aims to integrate niche security players into unified cybersecurity platforms, meeting enterprise demand for comprehensive, simplified solutions.
PE exits have surpassed $13 billion, supported by high-profile IPOs like SailPoint Technologies.
Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) are thriving, with over 120 deals totaling $9.2 billion closed so far in 2025.
Premium valuations continue for companies in cloud security, identity management, and advanced threat detection, with the median M&A transaction size at $109 million.
While public-to-private deals have slowed due to high public valuations, competition for top-tier assets remains intense.
A standout trend is the integration of artificial intelligence into cybersecurity strategies.
VC funding for AI-driven cybersecurity startups is accelerating, as organizations seek automated threat detection and faster response capabilities.
M&A activity in this AI segment, which surged in 2024, continues strongly in 2025 as strategic buyers race to acquire cutting-edge AI technologies that enhance cyber resilience.
